title: Long cord, more loops
hook: In the paper’s setup, which length knotted more often?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: The experiment used a 30cm box, one revolution per second and ten seconds of tumbling. Its short strings had no observed knots; three-metre strings knotted in 55% of the reported trials. The stage samples those observed frequencies with seed 17.

claims.text: Recall: Suppose 11 of 20 trials knot a 3 m string in a 30 cm box turning once per second for 10 seconds. What does that show? Correct answer: A 55% observed frequency in that setup; other setups need their own checks. 11 ÷ 20 = 55% is the observed frequency in this stipulated test. It neither guarantees an exact count in another run nor transfers unchanged to a different box, string or motion. This recall example is hypothetical, not an additional reported experiment.
